key_insight: GPT-4.1 can simulate personas to predict opinions with high accuracy, including election outcomes and some health beliefs.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLM-based persona simulation could help explore public attitudes toward vaccines and other health topics, but it is not a substitute for direct population evidence.
method: Used persona profiles from Columbia University’s Personas dataset to test state-level opinion prediction.
Applied GPT-4.1 to Pew Research Center’s American Trends Panel Wave 123 on medicine and healthcare beliefs.
Generated persona-based dialogues to assess whether outputs matched personality and background traits.
evidence_signal: The model correctly predicted 8 of 9 U.S. state election outcomes and reached up to 0.94 accuracy for beliefs about childhood vaccines.
watch_item: Outputs may reflect bias and the simulated conversations were less natural than human dialogue, so results need cautious interpretation.
paper_title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Persona Simulation in Opinion Prediction with GPT-4.1
